text:
rachel: Hey folks, planning a short customer visit next week that includes an overnight ferry + train. A few quick Qs before I book: 1) ferry cabin price includes dinner for passengers but not drinks  can I still claim per-diem for that travel day? 2) the vendor sent one invoice that includes catering for both company attendees and external partners who paid separately  how do I submit the invoice so finance reimburses only our portion? 3) if travel crosses midnight but is <24h total do we treat it as full travel day for per-diem? 4) I sometimes get only a digital e-ticket for regional trains  is that an acceptable receipt?

liz (People Ops): Short: 1) mark meals provided by the ferry as "provided" when you select per-diem; we deduct that meal portion, not the whole day. 2) split the vendor invoice into lines: attach the full invoice, then create one expense line for our catering share and mark the non-company attendee line as "non-reimbursable" or attach proof of partner payment. 3) per policy, if the trip includes an overnight and you are away overnight, you may claim per-diem for the travel day; if trip is <24h and no overnight, claim per actuals. 4) e-tickets/screenshots are fine  attach the confirmation email and the card/cc charge line.

rachel: for #2 the invoice is messy  vendor labeled items generically ("lunch x1, dinner x1") and we have a separate PO that lists attendees. do i add attendee names in the notes?

sara (Events): Yes please. Add a short mapping note and attach the attendee list or the PO. Example: "Invoice: catering total 2400 EUR - company attendees (12) = 1200 EUR - external guests paid separately: invoice split attached". If external guests already paid vendor, attach their payment confirmation if available.

rachel: if we split a dinner and i paid the whole catering with my card, can finance reimburse our share later?

josh (Finance): Yes. Upload the itemized invoice and your payment evidence. Create an expense for your out-of-pocket amount and add a note listing the split per person. If others owe you, attach Venmo/transfer proof when they pay you back; we only reimburse your company-eligible portion.

rachel: about the ferry included dinner  if drinks were on top and i paid for wine, is that reimbursable?

liz (People Ops): Alcohol on business meals is reimbursable if reasonable. For ferry-provided dinner, if wine was optional and you paid separately, submit the wine receipt and mark the base meal as company-provided. Finance may flag high alcohol totals.

rachel: partial-day per-diem example?

liz (People Ops): Paste into notes: 
```
Day 1: depart 18:00 - overnight ferry cabin (dinner provided by ferry - deduct dinner portion). Paid wine 15 EUR on personal card - requesting reimbursement for wine only.
Day 2: arrive 08:00 - train midday (e-ticket attached) - claiming per-diem for lunch + incidentals.
```

josh (Finance): Also attach currency conversion note if charges in local currency. We use posted bank rate; include screenshot of card posting if helpful. For messy vendor invoices, include a short line-by-line mapping in the expense notes to speed approval.

rachel: e-ticket for regional train is a QR PDF  i'll attach that + cc line. final: timeline for reimbursement?

josh (Finance): Standard ~2 payroll cycles after approval. If you tag expense "expedite" and it's for vendor prepayment or critical vendor payment, notify finance and People Ops; we can prioritize.

people-ops-bot: Travel policy link: https://redwoodintranet.company/travel-policy See sections: "Per-diem offsets for provided meals", "Vendor invoice splitting", and "E-receipts and regional transport".

rachel: great, thanks all. i'll post the invoice + attendee list when i get them.
